newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT-Dollar eyes more upside after rebound.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Dollar eyes more upside after rebound.

text.p: Dollar/mark, in a display of renewed strength after a test of the downside, may be set for a new rally all the way to 1.7423, the 1997 high, analysts said on Wednesday.

At 1320 EDT/1720 GMT, dollar/mark traded at 1.7315/25, versus 1.7267/70 at the open, and 1.7305/10 late on Tuesday. Dollar/yen was quoted at 113.41/46 vs. 113.10/20 at the open, and 113.28/33 late on Tuesday.
Dollar/mark initially fell below crucial support at 1.7275 all the way to 1.7225. The bounce off that level led a successful attack on 1.7325-mark resistance.
"We broke the 1.7275 level but bounced back through 1.7325," said MCM CurrencyWatch senior analyst Scott Siller, commenting on the dollar's push to an intraday high at 1.7335.
"A key level now is 1.7355. If we get through there, we'll try the recent highs again," predicted Siller, referring to the 1.7407 level on June 13 and the 39-month high of 1.7423, set on June 6.
"Dollar/mark may look a bit toppish, but overall, it has retained a relatively firm tone," added Siller who did not see a dollar/mark selloff unless a rising trendline coming in at 1.7175 is broken.

Chartists also noted that dollar/mark set lows in the 1.7265/75 area on Friday, Monday and Tuesday. They said it was important for the dollar to close on Wednesday above that triple bottom in order to preserve the upside.
Siller acknowledged the mark remained weak all around, with a test of 65.25 mark/yen still in the cards and sterling/mark eyeing the key psychological level of 2.85.
Sterling/mark has not traded above that level since Europe's Exchange Rate Mechanism crisis in August 1992.
At 1330 EDT/1730 GMT, mark/yen was quoted at 65.48/51 and sterling/mark at 2.8385/95.
"Even mark/Paris has a weak tone. We are at the low end of a two-three-week range but nothing great," Siller added.
Meanwhile, dollar/yen showed little stamina, consolidating in a narrow range after sliding from 114.85, Monday's high.
"It looks like a bearish consolidation, with a flat bottom, and a declining top," said Siller who stressed dollar/yen needs to take out 114.30 before targeting 115.80.
On the downside, chartists said 112.55 is a key support for dollar/yen -- the 62-percent retracement of the move from 110.62, the low on June 11, to 115.70, the high on June 12.
